# Skill: caveman-review

Write code review comments terse and actionable. One line per finding. Location, problem, fix. No throat-clearing.

## Rules

**Format:** `L<line>: <problem>. <fix>.` — or `<file>:L<line>: ...` when reviewing multi-file diffs.

**Severity prefix (optional, when mixed):**
- `🔴 bug:` — broken behavior, will cause incident
- `🟡 risk:` — works but fragile (race, missing null check, swallowed error)
- `🔵 nit:` — style, naming, micro-optim. Author can ignore
- `❓ q:` — genuine question, not a suggestion

**Drop:**
- "I noticed that...", "It seems like...", "You might want to consider..."
- "This is just a suggestion but..." — use `nit:` instead
- "Great work!", "Looks good overall but..." — say it once at the top, not per comment
- Restating what the line does — the reviewer can read the diff
- Hedging ("perhaps", "maybe", "I think") — if unsure use `q:`

**Keep:**
- Exact line numbers
- Exact symbol/function/variable names in backticks
- Concrete fix, not "consider refactoring this"
- The *why* if the fix isn't obvious from the problem statement

## Examples

❌ "I noticed that on line 42 you're not checking if the user object is null before accessing the email property. This could potentially cause a crash if the user is not found in the database. You might want to add a null check here."

✅ `L42: 🔴 bug: user can be null after .find(). Add guard before .email.`

❌ "It looks like this function is doing a lot of things and might benefit from being broken up into smaller functions for readability."

✅ `L88-140: 🔵 nit: 50-line fn does 4 things. Extract validate/normalize/persist.`

❌ "Have you considered what happens if the API returns a 429? I think we should probably handle that case."

✅ `L23: 🟡 risk: no retry on 429. Wrap in withBackoff(3).`

## Auto-Clarity

Drop terse mode for: security findings (CVE-class bugs need full explanation + reference), architectural disagreements (need rationale, not just a one-liner), and onboarding contexts where the author is new and needs the "why". In those cases write a normal paragraph, then resume terse for the rest.

## Boundaries

Reviews only — does not write the code fix, does not approve/request-changes, does not run linters. Output the comment(s) ready to paste into the PR. "stop caveman-review" or "normal mode": revert to verbose review style.

364:       add(`"${block.label}" (${spec.label}) can't have an inner workplace`, { blockId });
365:     }
366:     if (block.inner) validateLevel(block.inner, [...path, blockId], block, seen, issues);
367:   }
368: 
369:   if (parent) {
370:     const ports = blockPorts(parent);
371:     for (const [kind, list] of [
372:       ["block_input", ports.inputs],
373:       ["block_output", ports.outputs],
374:     ] as const) {
375:       for (const port of list) {
376:         const count = graph.blocks.filter((b) => b.kind === kind && b.params.port === port.id);
377:         if (count.length !== 1) {
378:           add(`Port "${port.label}" needs exactly one ${kind} block, found ${count.length}`);
379:         }
380:       }
381:       const valid = new Set(list.map((p) => p.id));
382:       for (const b of graph.blocks.filter((b) => b.kind === kind)) {
383:         if (!valid.has(String(b.params.port))) {
384:           add(`"${b.label}" points to a port the parent block doesn't have`, { blockId: b.id });
385:         }
386:       }
387:     }
388:   }
389: 
390:   const edgeIds = new Set<string>();
391:   const blocksById = new Map(graph.blocks.map((b) => [b.id, b]));
392:   for (const edge of graph.edges) {
393:     const ref = { edgeId: edge.id };
394:     if (edgeIds.has(edge.id)) add(`Edge id "${edge.id}" is used more than once`, ref);
395:     edgeIds.add(edge.id);
396:     const source = blocksById.get(edge.source);
397:     const target = blocksById.get(edge.target);
398:     if (!source || !target) {
399:       add(`Edge "${edge.id}" connects a block that isn't on this workplace`, ref);
400:       continue;
401:     }
402:     if (source === target) add(`Edge "${edge.id}" connects "${source.label}" to itself`, ref);
403:     if (!blockPorts(source).outputs.some((p) => p.id === edge.sourcePort)) {
404:       add(`"${source.label}" has no output "${edge.sourcePort}"`, ref);
405:     }
406:     if (!blockPorts(target).inputs.some((p) => p.id === edge.targetPort)) {
407:       add(`"${target.label}" has no input "${edge.targetPort}"`, ref);
408:     }
409:   }
410: 
411:   // Kahn's algorithm: every block must be reachable in topological order.
412:   const indegree = new Map(graph.blocks.map((b) => [b.id, 0]));
413:   for (const e of graph.edges) {
414:     if (indegree.has(e.target)) indegree.set(e.target, indegree.get(e.target)! + 1);
415:   }
416:   const queue = [...indegree].filter(([, d]) => d === 0).map(([id]) => id);
417:   let visited = 0;
418:   while (queue.length) {
419:     const id = queue.shift()!;
420:     visited++;
421:     for (const e of graph.edges.filter((e) => e.source === id)) {
422:       if (!indegree.has(e.target)) continue;
423:       const d = indegree.get(e.target)! - 1;
424:       indegree.set(e.target, d);
425:       if (d === 0) queue.push(e.target);
426:     }
427:   }
428:   if (visited < graph.blocks.length) add("The blocks on this workplace form a loop");
429: }

135: export function createDataflowStore(initial: WorkflowGraph = emptyGraph()) {
136:   let noticeId = 0;
137: 
138:   return createStore<DataflowState>()((set, get) => {
139:     /** Runs `update` on the open workplace; on error, shows it and leaves the state unchanged. */
140:     const edit = (update: (graph: WorkflowGraph) => WorkflowGraph): boolean => {
141:       try {
142:         const current = selectWorkplace(get());
143:         const next = update(current);
144:         if (next !== current) set({ root: updateGraphAt(get().root, get().path, () => next) });
145:         return true;
146:       } catch (err) {
147:         get().notify("error", message(err));
148:         return false;
149:       }
150:     };

152:     return {
153:       root: withSplitterWorkplaces(initial),
154:       path: [],
155:       selectedBlockIds: [],
156:       selectedEdgeIds: [],
157:       measured: {},
158:       notice: null,
159:       report: null,
160: 
161:       addBlock(kind, position) {
162:         const id = newBlockId(kind);
163:         const label = nextBlockLabel(get().root, BLOCK_SPECS[kind].label);
164:         const block = createBlock(kind, { id, label, position });
165:         if (edit((g) => ({ ...g, blocks: [...g.blocks, block] }))) {
166:           set({ selectedBlockIds: [id], selectedEdgeIds: [] });
167:         }
168:         return id;
169:       },
170: 
171:       applyNodeChanges(changes) {
172:         let selected = new Set(get().selectedBlockIds);
173:         let measured = get().measured;
174:         const removed: string[] = [];
175:         const ok = edit((graph) => {
176:           let g = graph;
177:           for (const c of changes) {
178:             if (c.type === "position" && c.position) g = moveBlock(g, c.id, c.position);
179:             else if (c.type === "dimensions" && c.dimensions) {
180:               measured = { ...measured, [c.id]: c.dimensions };
181:             } else if (c.type === "select") {
182:               selected = new Set(selected);
183:               if (c.selected) selected.add(c.id);
184:               else selected.delete(c.id);
185:             } else if (c.type === "remove") removed.push(c.id);
186:           }
187:           return removed.length ? removeBlocks(g, removed) : g;
188:         });
189:         if (!ok) return;
190:         for (const id of removed) selected.delete(id);
191:         set({ selectedBlockIds: [...selected], measured });
192:       },
193: 
194:       applyEdgeChanges(changes) {
195:         let selected = new Set(get().selectedEdgeIds);
196:         const removed = changes.filter((c) => c.type === "remove").map((c) => c.id);
197:         for (const c of changes) {
198:           if (c.type !== "select") continue;
199:           selected = new Set(selected);
200:           if (c.selected) selected.add(c.id);
201:           else selected.delete(c.id);
202:         }
203:         if (removed.length && !edit((g) => removeEdges(g, removed))) return;
204:         for (const id of removed) selected.delete(id);
205:         set({ selectedEdgeIds: [...selected] });
206:       },
207: 
208:       checkConnection(connection) {
209:         const c = toCoreConnection(connection);
210:         if (!c) return { ok: false, reason: "Connect an output port to an input port." };
211:         return checkConnection(selectWorkplace(get()), c);
212:       },
213: 
214:       connect(connection) {
215:         const c = toCoreConnection(connection);
216:         if (!c) {
217:           get().notify("error", "Connect an output port to an input port.");
218:           return false;
219:         }
220:         return edit((g) => connectPorts(g, c));
221:       },
222: 
223:       deleteSelection() {
224:         const graph = selectWorkplace(get());
225:         const blocks = graph.blocks
226:           .filter((b) => get().selectedBlockIds.includes(b.id) && !isBoundaryBlockKind(b.kind))
227:           .map((b) => b.id);
228:         const edges = get().selectedEdgeIds;
229:         if (edit((g) => removeEdges(removeBlocks(g, blocks), edges))) {
230:           set({ selectedBlockIds: [], selectedEdgeIds: [] });
231:         }
232:       },
233: 
234:       setParams(blockId, params) {
235:         const graph = selectWorkplace(get());
236:         const block = graph.blocks.find((b) => b.id === blockId);
237:         if (!block) return `Block "${blockId}" is not on this workplace`;
238:         try {
239:           const result = setBlockParams(graph, blockId, params);
240:           set({ root: updateGraphAt(get().root, get().path, () => result.graph) });
241:           const n = result.removedEdges.length;
242:           if (n > 0) {
243:             get().notify(
244:               "info",
245:               `Removed ${n} connection${n === 1 ? "" : "s"} from ports that no longer exist.`,
246:             );
247:           }
248:           return null;
249:         } catch (err) {
250:           return paramError(err, block.kind);
251:         }
252:       },
253: 
254:       renameBlock(blockId, label) {
255:         try {
256:           const graph = renameInGraph(selectWorkplace(get()), blockId, label);
257:           set({ root: updateGraphAt(get().root, get().path, () => graph) });
258:           return null;
259:         } catch (err) {
260:           return message(err);
261:         }
262:       },
263: 
264:       selectBlock(blockId) {
265:         set({ selectedBlockIds: blockId ? [blockId] : [], selectedEdgeIds: [] });
266:       },
267: 
268:       openInner(blockId) {
269:         const block = selectWorkplace(get()).blocks.find((b) => b.id === blockId);
270:         if (!block?.inner) {
271:           get().notify("error", `"${block?.label ?? blockId}" has no inner workplace.`);
272:           return;
273:         }
274:         set({ path: [...get().path, blockId], selectedBlockIds: [], selectedEdgeIds: [] });
275:       },
276: 
277:       goTo(depth) {
278:         if (depth < 0 || depth > get().path.length) return;
279:         set({ path: get().path.slice(0, depth), selectedBlockIds: [], selectedEdgeIds: [] });
280:       },
281: 
282:       openReport(blockId) {
283:         const block = selectWorkplace(get()).blocks.find((b) => b.id === blockId);
284:         if (!block) {
285:           get().notify("error", `Block "${blockId}" is not on this workplace.`);
286:           return;
287:         }
288:         set({ report: { blockId, path: [...get().path] } });
289:       },
290: 
291:       closeReport() {
292:         set({ report: null });
293:       },
294: 
295:       revealBlock(path, blockId) {
296:         try {
297:           if (!graphAt(get().root, path).blocks.some((b) => b.id === blockId)) {
298:             throw new Error(`Block "${blockId}" no longer exists.`);
299:           }
300:         } catch (err) {
301:           get().notify("error", message(err));
302:           return;
303:         }
304:         set({ path: [...path], selectedBlockIds: [blockId], selectedEdgeIds: [], report: null });
305:       },
306: 
307:       notify(tone, text) {
308:         set({ notice: { id: ++noticeId, tone, message: text } });
309:       },
310: 
311:       dismissNotice() {
312:         set({ notice: null });
313:       },
314:     };
315:   });
316: }

318: /** The editor's store. Lives for the whole app session, so switching tabs keeps the flow. */
319: export const dataflowStore = createDataflowStore();

321: /**

323:  * with useMemo (zustand 5 re-renders forever on selectors that return a new object every time).
324:  */
325: export function useDataflow<T>(selector: (state: DataflowState) => T): T {
326:   return useStore(dataflowStore, selector);
327: }

20: export function getWorkflowsDir(dataDir: string): string {

22: }
23: 
24: export function listWorkflows(dataDir: string): Workflow[] {
25:   const dir = getWorkflowsDir(dataDir);
26:   if (!existsSync(dir)) return [];
27: 
28:   const files = readdirSync(dir).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".json"));
29:   const workflows: Workflow[] = [];
30: 
31:   for (const file of files) {
32:     try {
33:       const content = readFileSync(join(dir, file), "utf8");
34:       workflows.push(withSplitterWorkplaces(Workflow.parse(JSON.parse(content))));
35:     } catch {
36:       // skip corrupted files
37:     }
38:   }
39: 
40:   return workflows.sort(
41:     (a, b) => new Date(b.updatedAt).getTime() - new Date(a.updatedAt).getTime(),
42:   );
43: }

45: export function getWorkflow(dataDir: string, id: string): Workflow {
46:   const dir = getWorkflowsDir(dataDir);
47:   const filePath = join(dir, `${id}.json`);
48: 
49:   if (!existsSync(filePath)) {
50:     throw new ReqflowError("not_found", `Workflow not found: ${id}`);
51:   }
52: 
53:   try {
54:     const content = readFileSync(filePath, "utf8");
55:     return withSplitterWorkplaces(Workflow.parse(JSON.parse(content)));
56:   } catch (err) {
57:     throw new ReqflowError("not_found", `Failed to parse workflow ${id}`);
58:   }
59: }

61: export function saveWorkflow(dataDir: string, input: WorkflowSave): Workflow {
62:   input = withSplitterWorkplaces(input);
63:   // Validate graph
64:   const issues = validateGraph({ blocks: input.blocks, edges: input.edges });
65:   if (issues.length > 0) {
66:     throw new ReqflowError(
67:       "invalid_input",
68:       `Workflow graph has ${issues.length} validation issue(s)`,
69:       issues,
70:     );
71:   }
72: 
73:   const dir = getWorkflowsDir(dataDir);
74:   if (!existsSync(dir)) {
75:     mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
76:   }
77: 
78:   const now = new Date().toISOString();
79:   let workflow: Workflow;
80: 
81:   if (input.id) {
82:     let existing: Workflow | null = null;
83:     try {
84:       existing = getWorkflow(dataDir, input.id);
85:     } catch {
86:       existing = null;
87:     }
88: 
89:     if (existing) {
90:       workflow = Workflow.parse({
91:         id: existing.id,
92:         name: input.name,
93:         description: input.description,
94:         scope: input.scope,
95:         blocks: input.blocks,
96:         edges: input.edges,
97:         version: existing.version + 1,
98:         createdAt: existing.createdAt,
99:         updatedAt: now,
100:       });
101:     } else {
102:       workflow = Workflow.parse({
103:         id: input.id,
104:         name: input.name,
105:         description: input.description,
106:         scope: input.scope,
107:         blocks: input.blocks,
108:         edges: input.edges,
109:         version: 1,
110:         createdAt: now,
111:         updatedAt: now,
112:       });
113:     }
114:   } else {
115:     workflow = Workflow.parse({
116:       id: newId("wf"),
117:       name: input.name,
118:       description: input.description,
119:       scope: input.scope,
120:       blocks: input.blocks,
121:       edges: input.edges,
122:       version: 1,
123:       createdAt: now,
124:       updatedAt: now,
125:     });
126:   }
127: 
128:   const filePath = join(dir, `${workflow.id}.json`);
129:   const tmpPath = join(dir, `${workflow.id}.${Date.now()}.tmp`);
130:   writeFileSync(tmpPath, JSON.stringify(workflow, null, 2), "utf8");
131:   renameSync(tmpPath, filePath);
132: 
133:   return workflow;
134: }

137:   const dir = getWorkflowsDir(dataDir);
138:   const filePath = join(dir, `${id}.json`);

140:     unlinkSync(filePath);
141:   }

20:   }
21:   if (err instanceof ZodError) {

23:   }

25:   return { code: "internal", message: String(err) };

28: /** Pure (Electron-free) so it can be unit-tested: route one IPC call to its handler. */
29: export async function dispatch(
30:   handlers: ReqflowHandlers,
31:   namespace: string,
32:   method: string,
33:   args: unknown[],
34: ): Promise<IpcResult<unknown>> {
35:   const ns = (handlers as unknown as Record<string, Record<string, unknown> | undefined>)[
36:     namespace
37:   ];
38:   const fn = ns?.[method];

40:     return {
